title: Sin as disease; healed by grace and Christ's bruise (Ps 103; Mal 4)
source_text: XIII. Peccata quoque nostra comparantur morbis atque vulneribus, quibus animae nostrae aegrae & sauciae sunt: & propterea Deus dicitur per gratiam suam nostras infirmitates, sive morbos sanare. Quod Dei beneficium agnoscit & celebrat David, Psal. 103. Benedic, inquit, anima mea Domino, & noli oblivisci omnes retributiones ejus. Qui propitiatur omnibus iniquitatibus tuis; Qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas. Ac quia Christus ille est qui morte sua nobis gratiam illam impetravit, dicimur ejus livore sanati, Cujus livore, inquit Petrus, sanati estis. Et propterea Malachias etiam Propheta vocat illum justitiae solem, in cujus alis, id est, radiis sanitas est: Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum sol justitiae, & sanitas in pennis sive in alis ejus. Mal. 4.
pass_a_gloss: Our sins also are compared to diseases and wounds by which our souls are sick and wounded: and therefore God is said by his grace to heal our infirmities or diseases. Which benefit of God David acknowledges and celebrates (Psalm 103): Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his recompenses. Who is propitious to all your iniquities; Who heals all your infirmities. And because Christ is the one who by his death obtained that grace for us, we are said to be healed by his bruise: By whose bruise, says Peter, you were healed. And therefore the Prophet Malachi also calls him the sun of righteousness, in whose wings, that is, rays, there is healing: The sun of righteousness shall rise for you who fear my name, and healing in his feathers or wings (Malachi 4).
pass_b_english: Sin is also disease and wound; God heals infirmities (Psalm 103).
By Christ's bruise we are healed; Malachi's sun of righteousness brings healing in his wings (Malachi 4).
